claims.text: Iranian missiles struck/damaged a US base in Kuwait (headline 'scar Kuwait base'; Press TV images)
claims.note: Press TV headline: new images reveal severe destruction at US base in Kuwait after Iranian strikes. Press TV page returned 503; only the headline is relied on.

claims.text: Ahmed al-Mansoor, 27, Yemeni-born contractor with shrapnel in his left thigh, writing from a field hospital in Al-Ahmadi
claims.note: No such person in sourceRefs or web search; invented character.

claims.text: Base named 'Camp Arif Al-Bayan'
claims.note: No such base found; reported Iranian strikes in Kuwait in Sep 2026 named Ali Al Salem and Ahmed Al-Jaber air bases. Invented.

claims.text: The strike happened on September 18
claims.note: Press TV headline gives no date; no source found for an 18 Sep strike.

claims.text: The strike left three Americans dead and dozens wounded, confirmed by Press TV footage
claims.note: Press TV headline mentions destruction only, not casualties. Web search found no confirmed US deaths from a September 2026 strike in Kuwait (confirmed deaths were in March).

claims.text: $2,400 a week in lost wages; drones humming over the desert
claims.note: Detail of invented character.

claims.text: Ahvaz medicine shortage reported by SCMP; shortages deepened as ports sit idle under shipping bans
claims.note: SCMP headline supports only 'Iran medicine shortages deepen as war, shipping restrictions continue'. Ahvaz, idle ports and 'shipping bans' are not in the headline; article blocked (403).

claims.text: Dialysis fluid, insulin and antibiotics rationed; mother travels three hours for a vial of insulin
claims.note: Not in source headline; invented detail.

claims.text: Earl Spencer's new biography of Diana, unveiled by the BBC, drags the royals back into grief
claims.note: BBC headline: 'Earl Spencer's Diana book opens old wounds royals would rather forget'. Supports a Spencer book about Diana; 'unveiled by the BBC' and 'biography' are not supported. Marked wrong on review: the book is not a BBC release, and "biography" is not in the source. Only the existence of a Spencer book about Diana is supported.

claims.text: Book reveals a 1995 private letter from Diana quoting 'the world will never let me breathe'
claims.note: Quote and letter not found anywhere; invented.

claims.text: Petitions to rename the 'Princess Diana Memorial Fund'
claims.note: Nothing found; invented.

claims.text: Mix-up cost them $12,000 in legal fees

edits.headline: Florida couple sue Jacksonville fertility clinic over IVF sperm mix-up
edits.subheadline: The suit says DNA testing found a 0% probability that the husband is their daughter's biological father, IBTimes UK reported.
editorialBody: Natalie and Joshua Strong have sued Brown Fertility in Jacksonville, Florida, saying it used another man's sperm to create their daughter's embryo, the New York Post reported on 19 September.

The suit, filed in Duval County Circuit Court, names the clinic's founder, Dr. Samuel Brown, and 10 other defendants. It says DNA testing found a 0% probability that Joshua Strong is the girl's father, IBTimes UK reported. The girl was born in June 2025.
Iran's Press TV published images it said showed severe destruction at a US base in Kuwait after Iranian strikes.
Medicine shortages in Iran have deepened as the war and shipping restrictions continue, the South China Morning Post reported.

Residents near the Inglewood Oil Field in Los Angeles may receive payments under AB 1661, Wired reported. The bill would pay up to $5,000 each to 1,000 households from $5 million in penalties on oil wells, Capital B reported.
Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces had taken Maryevka and Gulevo in the Donetsk region, Sputnik reported.
The European Union urged the United States to lift its travel ban on the Palestinian delegation to the UN General Assembly meeting, Al Jazeera reported.
